summary: Parks, Forestry and Recreation operates four stadiums that are host to frequent community events and large sporting events. As is the case with other large sporting venues in Toronto, there is often an expectation that alcohol consumption at these stadiums will be an option for those who choose to consume. The current version of the Municipal Alcohol Policy does not allow the sale and consumption of alcohol in tiered seating at City owned and operated stadiums. Event organizers are currently limited to designated areas of the stadium for the sale and consumption of alcohol. Parks, Forestry and Recreation has received additional stakeholder input and has been advised that this restriction could limit the game experience and potential growth of certain sports and organizations. Parks, Forestry and Recreation has consulted with Toronto Public Health and determined that it may be acceptable to approve exemptions, provided the event and event organizer meet specific criteria, as outlined below, to encourage and support responsible drinking practices for individuals who choose to consume alcohol. The event and applicant must demonstrate that all tiered seating requirements identified by Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario as outlined in the Special Occasion Permit application process, have been satisfied. decided: City Council on May 22, 23 and 24, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council authorize the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to provide exemptions, in consultation with the Chief Medical Officer of Health, to allow the sale and consumption of alcohol in tiered seating at stadiums, in accordance with requirements of the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario, Municipal Alcohol Policy and Parks, Forestry and Recreation permits.
